title: Kula burn scar fencing and native replanting
summary: The Kula Community Watershed Alliance is fencing and replanting the steep burn scar, with over a thousand plants in the fully fenced upper section and over 30,000 growing in its nursery. Over 200 deer have been removed in the past year, and the group hopes more fencing by the end of the year will let it plant hundreds of thousands of native plants. On September 9, the chair offered to contact the group about a volunteer app in development.

timeline.text: The chair will contact the watershed group next week about a volunteer app that is in development.
The group aims to restore an ancient ecosystem that will one day become an old growth forest.
The speaker said more native plants now grow in the gulch than before the fire.

A Kula watershed group is fencing and replanting a steep area that burned in the fire.
A member with the Kula Community Watershed Alliance said the group is putting deer fencing around the Kula burn scar.

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: And we're going up to collect, we're propagating the seeds, and we're getting ready to have our first planting late next month.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: The Alliance gives its timeline: native seeds are being collected and propagated, and the first planting on the burn scar is set for late the following month.

source.title: Upcountry Community Meeting on Hazard Mitigation & Recovery: February 29, 2024

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: We just received a grant, as Yuki Lei mentioned. Part of that grant is going to include a community greenhouse, so that we can actually grow our own and kind of build community around that and educate around that. It also includes stabilization, fencing, planting, and you know...
fromCommunityMeetings.about: The Alliance explains that its new grant pays for a community greenhouse, stabilization, fencing and planting on about 25 acres of the Kula burn scar.

source.title: Upcountry Community Meeting on Hazard Mitigation & Recovery: February 29, 2024

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: We went through the entire winter without anything, except for what we could do ourselves. To me, that's unacceptable.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: The Alliance describes the community waiting since November for $2.7 million in federal emergency watershed erosion-control work on the Kula burn area.

source.title: Upcountry Community Meeting on Hazard Mitigation & Recovery: February 29, 2024

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: Today or actually yesterday, we started soil stabilization on our eighth acre in Kula. And we're just working in places where we understand there won't be government support through the NRCS Emergency Watershed Protection Program.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: The fire survivor-led watershed group reports it has begun soil stabilization on its eighth acre of the Kula burn area, filling gaps left by federal programs.

source.title: Kula Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: January 31, 2024

fromCommunityMeetings.quote: So, extremely important that we prevent runoff, sedimentation laws, and all the things. And we're working with Department of Health on the Clean Water Act funding. The Alliance has been written into the Ma'alai'a Bay Watershed Management Plan.
fromCommunityMeetings.about: The group explains why burn scar stabilization matters for downstream waters and how it is seeking Clean Water Act funding for the work.
